initial_messages.content: Explain how the water cycle moves water between the ocean, atmosphere, and land. Use three short paragraphs suitable for a general audience.

initial.text:
The water cycle, also known as the hydrologic cycle, is a continuous process that moves water around the Earth between the ocean, atmosphere, and land. It all starts with evaporation from the surface of oceans, seas, and other bodies of water. Heat from the sun causes water to evaporate into the air as water vapor. Plants also release water vapor into the atmosphere through a process called transpiration. As water vapor rises and cools, it condenses into tiny droplets, forming clouds in the sky. 

When enough water droplets come together, they become heavy and fall back to the Earth as precipitation in the form of rain, snow, sleet, or hail. Some of this precipitation falls directly back into oceans and lakes. But much of it falls on land, where it can soak into the soil as groundwater, flow over the surface as runoff into rivers and streams, or collect in puddles, ponds, and wetlands. Water that soaks into the ground can eventually make its way back to oceans and lakes via underground channels.
